clue.text: Something wicked and frivolous helps dispel the gloom

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun answer: the clue reads as 'something that helps dispel the gloom'

parts.note: a wax stick fitted with a wick is literally 'wicked', a play on the word for evil
light can mean frivolous, not serious, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A wicked, frivolous person somehow lifts everyone's dark mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like a moral judgement, but it means 'having a wick'. The definition borrows 'Something' from the start of the clue in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft illumination from wax tapers lifts darkness in a room.

clue.text: Eager to work in silver

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the working piece sits within the symbol for silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: Someone keen to take up silversmithing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe keen, excited anticipation; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Experts in digitally recorded evidence

explanation.surface: Forensic specialists who handle digital records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally' looks like computing, but it means 'by the fingers': dabs is slang for fingerprints. A dab hand is an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled person is a dab or dab hand; police slang calls fingerprints dabs.

clue.text: Member in neat outfit showing good taste

indicators.note: 'in' places the limb word inside the rearranged letters
to outfit is to fit out or rig up afresh, so the letters of 'neat' are reorganised

parts.note: a leg is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: A club member wears a tidy outfit that shows refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' makes EANT from NEAT, and 'in' puts LEG inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful, refined style is a mark of discerning taste.

clue.text: I'm a leader of Muslims

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of 'Muslims'

explanation.surface: A cleric introduces himself as head of a Muslim congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer leader in a mosque bears this title; the whole clue is his self-introduction.

clue.text: Getting a small rise, I'll get in some wine

indicators.note: to get in is to go inside, so the contracted word enters the wine

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy says a little lift will come from fetching some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British name for Rhine white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hummock or knoll is a little rise in the ground.

clue.text: An actor in Midlands town playing Romeo

parts.note: Dudley is a town in the West Midlands of England

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of 'Romeo' being toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer from a Midlands town takes the role of Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: DUDLEY is a town near Birmingham; 'playing' rearranges ROMEO into MOORE, giving the comic actor and pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: The British comedian starred in films such as Arthur and 10.

clue.text: Struck by the way a sale may be concluded

definitions.text: the way a sale may be concluded

explanation.surface: A bidder is hit at an auction as the sale closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored by a blow; at auction a lot is sold when the hammer falls on it.

clue.text: Go for a short walk

explanation.surface: Advice to take a brief stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Your turn is your go in a game; a turn round the park is a stroll.

clue.text: Not a single mistake by serviceman

definitions.text: Not a single mistake by serviceman

parts.words: Not a single mistake by serviceman
parts.note: 'serviceman' suggests a soldier, but here it is a tennis server, and two consecutive missed serves form one error, hence 'not a single' mistake

explanation.surface: A soldier commits more than one blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis two failed serves in a row lose the point.

clue.text: Smart fellow gets the beer and last of the cognac

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of 'cognac'

explanation.surface: A dapper man orders a beer and finishes off the brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart fellow' points to the phrase smart alec, a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'smart alec' names a cocky know-it-all, so the name alone stands for him.

clue.text: Top dog of the Variety Club?

definitions.text: Top dog of the Variety Club?

parts.words: Top dog of the Variety Club?
parts.note: the charity Variety Club calls its leader by a circus-style title, and a dog barks

explanation.surface: Who heads a show-business charity?
explanation.walkthrough: The Variety Club is a show-business charity whose president carries a title from the circus world.
explanation.definitionFit: The charity's president is styled with a fairground showman's title.

clue.text: Call round to set up joint management

indicators.note: to set up is to arrange, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Phoning round to establish a shared management scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sets of controls let two people share the steering, as in a learner's car.

clue.text: He escaped to become famous

parts.note: describes a performer whose fame rested on getting free of chains, locks and tanks

explanation.surface: A fugitive who made his name by fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian-American showman won fame as an escapologist.

clue.text: Gershwin tune heartless and angry

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

indicators.note: removing the heart of 'tune' leaves its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Gershwin song that lacks soul makes the listener cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and cross are synonyms of the clue word.

clue.text: Churchman gets a pass, yet goes astray

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of 'yet' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cleric is let through, but still loses his way.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar server or assistant in church services is a lay helper of the clergy.

clue.text: It is struck by forgers

parts.note: 'forgers' suggests counterfeiters, but here they are smiths who forge metal on an iron block

explanation.surface: Fraudsters taking a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith hammers hot iron on this heavy iron block.

clue.text: Jumbo jet propeller?

parts.note: 'Jumbo' suggests an airliner, but it is an elephant, which squirts a jet of water from its nose

explanation.surface: What drives a large airliner?
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long nose sprays water like a hose.

clue.text: Pat her on the knee

indicators.note: 'on' says the girl's name follows Pat, so removing Pat from the kneecap leaves her

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap
taken as written, as a name

explanation.surface: Someone gives a girl a friendly tap on her knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a verb but is a name: PAT followed by the girl's name makes PATELLA, the kneecap.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a woman, so the pronoun can define it.

clue.text: State of mind caused by a turn of fate

indicators.note: turning a word round reads its letters backwards

parts.note: doom is an unhappy fate

explanation.surface: A change in fortune alters one's outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Temper or humour, as in a bad temper, is a passing frame of mind.

clue.text: Forbearing Scot I maddened

indicators.note: driven mad suggests the letters of 'Scot I' going wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient Scotsman says I drove him mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring hardship without complaint, as the ancient philosophers taught.

clue.text: Possibly ignores an Italian man's entitlement

indicators.note: 'possibly' hints that the letters of 'ignores' might form something else

explanation.surface: Maybe someone disregards an Italian's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitlement' looks like a right, but it means a title: the Italian equivalent of Mister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian form of address for a gentleman, like Mr or Sir.

clue.text: La Costa resort by the sea

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of 'La Costa' are reshuffled

explanation.surface: La Costa is a holiday resort on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreline places lie beside the ocean.

clue.text: Camera for young girl who promises to do her best

definitions.text: young girl who promises to do her best

explanation.surface: A photographic gift for a junior Guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The Box Brownie was a cheap Kodak camera; Brownies are the junior Girl Guides, whose promise is to do their best.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic Kodak box camera, and a junior member of the Girl Guides.

clue.text: Wild blow leads to dispute with non-intellectual

indicators.note: wild implies the letters of 'blow' are thrown about

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A wild punch starts a fight with an uncultured man.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated in taste, the opposite of highbrow.

clue.text: Find fault with the price

explanation.surface: Complaining about the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: To rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate or scold someone; and a charge or fee per unit.

clue.text: Seen in church when spring is over before Easter starts

indicators.note: turned over, a word reads backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of 'Easter'

explanation.surface: A church visit after the spring season, just before Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns SPA to APS; 'before' places it ahead of the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed recess at the east end of a church holds the altar.

clue.text: Animal with arms raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: gats is slang for guns

explanation.surface: A beast with its hands up.
explanation.walkthrough: GAT is old gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal.

clue.text: An outstanding leader of men

explanation.surface: A remarkable chief of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means sticking out: a boss is a raised knob, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A protruding stud or knob; and a manager or chief.

clue.text: Contest the capitalistic thesis

explanation.surface: Arguing against free-market theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament or match; and the rivalry between firms that free-market thinking holds up as its principle.

clue.text: Mark goes back to school

indicators.note: going back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a note is a mark, as in 'of note'

explanation.surface: Mark returns to his school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a boy's name, but it is a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Lineages got from him? Yes

indicators.note: 'from' says the answer's letters come out of 'Lineages got' rearranged

explanation.surface: Do family trees come from him? Indeed they do.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher of family descent traces ancestry and pedigrees.
